content_voiceover: This slide drills into the efficacy numbers from the pivotal first line phase 3 trials. Spleen volume reduction of 35 percent, called SVR35, and total symptom score reduction of 50 percent, called TSS50, at week 24 are the two key endpoints used across these studies. COMFORT one compared ruxolitinib to best available therapy and showed 41.9 percent SVR35 and 45.9 percent TSS50, in patients with platelets at least 100. COMFORT two used a similar design against best available therapy but only reported SVR35, at 32 percent. JAKARTA tested fedratinib against placebo in a similar platelet population and achieved 37 percent SVR35 and 40 percent TSS50. PERSIST one tested pacritinib against best available therapy with no platelet restriction at all, which is its defining feature, but showed lower response rates, around 19 percent for both endpoints. Finally SIMPLIFY one was a non-inferiority trial comparing momelotinib against ruxolitinib itself, in patients with platelets at least 50, and momelotinib was non-inferior for spleen response but numerically lower for symptom response. The key exam point is that pacritinib is the only drug in this group studied with truly no platelet floor, making it the go to choice for severely thrombocytopenic patients.
keypoints: COMFORT one and two, ruxolitinib vs BAT, platelets over 100, SVR35 32 to 42 percent
JAKARTA, fedratinib vs placebo, SVR35 37 percent, TSS50 40 percent
PERSIST one, pacritinib vs BAT, no platelet limit, response around 19 percent
SIMPLIFY one, momelotinib non-inferior to ruxolitinib, platelets over 50
Pacritinib uniquely has no platelet count restriction in its pivotal trial
keypoint_voiceover: Remember the platelet thresholds. COMFORT one and two and JAKARTA required platelets over 100 or 50 respectively. SIMPLIFY one required platelets over 50 and showed momelotinib is non-inferior to ruxolitinib for spleen response. PERSIST one stands out because pacritinib had no platelet floor, giving roughly 19 percent SVR35 and TSS50 even in severely thrombocytopenic patients.
